units.translation: b. Jason especially desires to learn two things from Phineus: first, how he might sail back through the Symplegades on his return; second, how he might reach Colchis after sailing across so great a sea. He indicated the difficulty of the voyage by saying that Colchis lies at the ends of the earth and of the Pontus. P
c. Aea, a Colchian city: Aea is a city of Colchis; it lies at the ends of the inhabited world.
421-22a. Since a god: From Aea, he says, that is, from the Colchians, a god will guide you, and for those sailing to Aea there will be many escorts in general.
b. From Aea: Another voyage, he says, will be yours from Aea. He says this because they will not return through the Symplegades.
423-24. But, friends, take thought: Keep in mind, he says, the cunning help from Aphrodite.
431-32. "But as far as they drove" instead of "as far as they traveled." P
434. Cave of Dicte: To the mountain of Crete. "Crags"
but according to some, the broken fragments of mountains; but according to the lexicographers, all mountains are called crags.

438. "Surely then someone": The "ara" is used ethically, meaning "as it seems." And in the Odyssey (17.454): "You did not, it seems, have wits to match your appearance." And Hesiod (Works and Days 11): "There was not, it seems, only one race of Strifes," meaning there was not, as it seems, only one Strife.
441-42. "But if with eyes": But if one of the gods should make you see again, I would rejoice as much as if I were saved to my fatherland. L
445. "They are smoldering beneath": They are smoldering, that is, they have been dimmed by suffering. "To smolder beneath" also means to burn gently underneath, as if they have been burnt underneath.
451-52. "Who even before day after day": Who continually came to him. The order: bringing a portion of their own food. Lm (P)

456-57. "And with them came Paraebius": Apollonius says that Paraebius was a friend of Phineus, but others say he was a faithful slave. Those around Paraebius, he says, rejoiced when they saw the heroes.
458-60a. "Himself": Phineus, clearly. Lg

b. For Phineus himself had spoken beforehand and foretold to Paraebius the coming of the heroes. One must connect the preposition "hypo" with "emythesato" and take it as "pro" (before); just as "hypeipon" (Aristophanes, Wasps 55) is used for "proeipon" (having said beforehand). P
c. "In the Thynian land": He again called the region around the Bosporus Thynian (cf. v. 177). Lm
d. Note that he said "Thynian land," in which Phineus dwelt, as being a part of Thrace which is called Thynis. P
470. "Fate": Here, fortune. Lg (P)
471-75a. "For whenever he had toiled most": Paraebius,
he says, paying for his father's sin, was always in want of livelihood, even if he toiled exceedingly.
b. "Want": Lack, poverty, need. Lg (P)
